comments.author: eth0up
comments.why_zh: 阿拉斯加荒野中即兴发挥的手工木作，能启发观众。
comments.quote_zh: 只有最无动于衷的人才会不觉得它鼓舞人心
comments.text_zh: 我很惊讶这里居然没有评论提到老 Dick Proenneke——在我看来，他那富有创造力、即兴发挥的木工活，将在人类存续的整个期间都堪称传奇。对大多数人来说，他的作品并不实用，也不能直接照搬，但只有最无动于衷的人才会不觉得它鼓舞人心。[LINK] [VIDEO] Alone In The Wilderness, Part I
comments.text: I was surprised to not see any comments here referencing ol' Dick Proenneke, whose creative, improvisational woodwork will, in my opinion, remain legendary for the duration of humanity. For most, his work won't be practical or directly applicable, but only for the most indifferent will it fail to be inspirational. [LINK] [VIDEO] Alone In The Wilderness, Part I

comments.text: This reminds me of some awesome documentary footage of a man who built a cabin in the Alaskan wilderness: [VIDEO] Alone in the Wilderness - Dick Proenneke The same dry commentary made riveting by insightful and sometimes whimsical observations, the same hardship usually effortlessly overcome, and of course the same solitary strength of a middle-aged man. Both stories make me a bit envious, and inspire me to create a little more with my hands.

comments.author: chrissnell
comments.why_zh: 一部关于独居阿拉斯加木屋者的精彩PBS纪录片
comments.quote_zh: 有一部关于他的 PBS 纪录片非常精彩，YouTube 上就能看
comments.text_zh: 我有过一罐用了好几年的酵母 starter，是从 Dick Proenekke 保存的那罐传下来的[1]。他独自住在阿拉斯加荒野深处一间亲手盖的木屋里。他每天做酸种煎饼，而他最初的那罐 starter 来自镇上的一位朋友。跟这个人有关的某个人在卖这种 starter（装在一把木勺上），你可以买来[2]，培养出自己的一支后代。如果感兴趣，有一部关于他的 PBS 纪录片非常精彩，YouTube 上就能看：[3] [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I had a starter for several years that was descended from the one kept by Dick Proenekke [1]. He lived alone in a cabin that he built himself--by hand--deep in the Alaskan bush. He made sourdough pancakes daily and his original starter came from a friend of his back in town. Someone related to this person sells the starter (on a wooden spoon) that you can buy [2] and use to create your own descendant. There's a fascinating PBS documentary on him that you can watch on YouTube, if you're interested: [3] [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [VIDEO]

comments.author: livueta
comments.story_title: 'Into The Wild' bus removed from Alaska wilderness
comments.why_zh: Proenneke 以真正的技艺，拍摄了自己用当地材料盖木屋的过程
comments.quote_zh: 他带着一台 8mm 摄影机，拍下了自己的大量工作，包括几乎完全用当地材料盖起自己的木屋
comments.text_zh: 我一直把 Dick Proenneke[1] 看作 McCandless 本可以成为、也应该成为的样子。尽管两人尝试的是类似的事（尽可能脱离文明，不过 Proenneke 没有走到那么极端），但 Proenneke 确实有准备，也有在荒野中过好日子所需的手艺——总的来说，这家伙是个强得离谱的户外人，此外还有一流的木工/木作[2]/各种临时凑合的本事。最棒的是，他带着一台 8mm 摄影机，拍下了自己的大量工作，包括几乎完全用当地材料盖起自己的木屋。这些影像最终成了（有 PBS 参与的？）纪录片《Alone in the Wilderness》[3]。--- [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [VIDEO]（部分内容）
comments.text: I've always thought of Dick Proenneke[1] as what McCandless could have/should have been. Despite attempting a similar thing (go detach from civilization as much as possible, though Proenneke didn't take it to the same extreme), Proenneke was actually prepared and talented in the kinds of crafts necessary to have a good life in the wilderness - guy was a crazy-good outdoorsman in general, on top of great carpentry/woodworking[2]/general jury-rigging. The best part is that he took an 8mm camera and filmed a lot of his work, including building his cabin from almost entirely indigenous materials. Those films ended up as the (PBS-involved?) documentary Alone in the Wilderness [3]. --- [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [VIDEO] (partial)

comments.author: dredmorbius
comments.story_title: For 40 Years, This Russian Family Was Cut Off From All Human Contact
comments.why_zh: 展现 Proenneke 非凡的木工手艺和荒野生活。
comments.quote_zh: Dick 的手艺（他在文明世界生活时当过木匠）令人惊叹
comments.text_zh: YouTube 上至少有一部分：[VIDEO] [LINK] Dick 的手艺（他在文明世界生活时当过木匠）令人惊叹，不过他仍与外界保持着定期联系，包括定期收到补给。同样有意思的是，他依赖那些自己无法复制的钢制工具：锯子、锛子、刨子、斧头、炉子、锅碗瓢盆。他确实把其中许多东西背了进去，大多数没有手柄（手柄是他在现场用木头做的）。Proenneke 虽然富有创造力、极其独立，但绝非自给自足。
comments.text: YouTube has at least a portion of this: [VIDEO] [LINK] Dick's capabilities (he had been a carpenter when living in civilization) were amazing, though he remained in periodic contact with the rest of civilization, including receiving regular supplies. It's also interesting to note his reliance on steel tools that he wasn't capable of replacing: saws, adzes, planes, axes, stove, pots and pans. He did pack in many of these, most without handles (he fashioned those from wood on site). While creative and highly independent, Proenneke was by no means self-sufficient.
